title: deploygate · LGTM
description: Sigil evaluation throughput and latency, followed by HTTP load measurements and policy decisions across Mimir metrics, Tempo traces, Loki logs and Pyroscope profiles. Team filters evaluations and policy panels; Load run filters k6 panels. Profiles cover the whole process.

panels.title: Service up
panels.description: The latest Alloy scrape of deploygate, stored in Mimir. DOWN means the scrape failed; no data means the pipeline has not delivered a sample.

panels.title: Deploy decisions
panels.description: Deployment decisions in the selected time range and team. Requests rejected during access evaluation are counted in evaluation errors.

panels.title: Failed reloads
panels.description: Bundles rejected in the selected range. Each one kept the previous bundle serving; the service log and POST /api/v1/policies/reload show the compile error.

panels.title: Last successful reload
panels.description: Seconds since the older of the team and access bundles last loaded, so a stuck bundle can't hide behind a fresh one. With polling on, it resets every time a policies directory changes; a failed reload leaves it growing while the previous bundle keeps serving.

panels.title: Evaluations / second
panels.description: Observed rate of completed p.Eval calls across access and deploy policies over the rate window. Includes successful and failed evaluations. A deployment can contribute two evaluations. Follows Team, independently of Load run. This is achieved throughput at the current offered load.

panels.title: Evaluations in selected range
panels.description: Estimated number of completed p.Eval calls in the dashboard time range, summed across both stages. Uses counter increases to account for process restarts; scrape extrapolation can produce a fractional estimate.

panels.title: Mean access evaluation
panels.description: Mean elapsed time around p.Eval over the selected time range. Computed from histogram sum divided by count, weighted across the selected teams. HTTP decoding, policy loading, response formatting and logging happen outside this timer. No evaluations means no latency value.

panels.title: Mean deploy evaluation
panels.description: Mean elapsed time around p.Eval over the selected time range. Computed from histogram sum divided by count, weighted across the selected teams. HTTP decoding, policy loading, response formatting and logging happen outside this timer. No evaluations means no latency value.

panels.title: Evaluation throughput by stage
panels.description: Completed p.Eval calls per second for each stage, including failed evaluations. The access endpoint evaluates access alone; a deployment also evaluates deploy if access succeeds. Uses histogram counts so multiple grants cannot inflate throughput.

panels.title: Evaluations within 100 µs
panels.description: Fraction of completed p.Eval calls taking at most 100 microseconds, using the exact 0.0001-second histogram bucket for each stage. This is an observed latency distribution, not an SLO. No traffic produces no latency value.

panels.title: Access evaluation latency
panels.description: Elapsed time around p.Eval for the access policy. Quantiles are estimated from the histogram buckets, whose lowest boundary is 50 microseconds. Use the mean above for the sum/count measurement. Follows Team; excludes HTTP handling, policy loading and response formatting.

panels.title: Deploy evaluation latency
panels.description: Elapsed time around p.Eval for the deploy policy. Quantiles are estimated from the histogram buckets, whose lowest boundary is 50 microseconds. Use the mean above for the sum/count measurement. Follows Team; excludes HTTP handling, policy loading and response formatting.

panels.title: k6 · request rate
panels.description: Achieved HTTP request rate per run. Compare with the configured arrival rate; dropped iterations below expose generator saturation.

panels.title: k6 · incorrect outcomes
panels.description: Fraction of iterations with an unexpected status or policy result, cumulative within each run. Expected denials, conflicts and asserts count as correct. Zero is the goal.

panels.title: k6 · HTTP p95 by request
panels.description: Cumulative p95 for each request series within its run. Values are exported in seconds. These are separate percentiles, not a combined percentile; use the JSON report for the full-run p95. Only expected responses are included here; transport and correctness failures remain visible in the incorrect-outcomes panel.

panels.title: k6 · HTTP p99 by request
panels.description: Cumulative p99 for each request series within its run. Includes the network, decoding, both applicable policy stages and telemetry. See the JSON report for the overall p99. Only expected responses are included here; transport and correctness failures remain visible in the incorrect-outcomes panel.

panels.title: k6 · dropped iterations
panels.description: Reported cumulative dropped iterations observed within the selected time range. k6 only emits this counter when it drops work, so retain the last observed count. Zero is shown only for runs with iteration samples. Check the JSON report for the completed run total.

targets.expr: sum by (testid) (max_over_time(k6_dropped_iterations_total{testid=~"${load_run:regex}"}[$__range])) or on (testid) (0 * sum by (testid) (max_over_time(k6_iterations_total{testid=~"${load_run:regex}"}[$__range])))

panels.title: k6 · active virtual users
panels.description: Active virtual users reported by k6. Increase MAX_VUS only when the generator needs more concurrency, and check the load generator resources too.

panels.title: Grants by role
panels.description: Roles granted per second by the AccessGrant policy, stacked by role and reason. It's a collect all kind, so one request can grant several roles, and a request that grants none adds nothing here.

panels.title: Decisions by outcome
panels.description: Deploy decisions per second, stacked by decision and reason. Failed deploy evaluations count here with the fallback the host acts on (deny no_rule_matched) and also under Evaluation errors; a request that fails in the access stage never reaches the deploy policy.

panels.title: Evaluation errors
panels.description: Failed evaluations per second by stage (access or deploy) and kind. assertion is usually a bad request: an input assert, or the access guardrails' separation-of-duties assert. conflict in the access stage is an actor granted two exclusive roles (409); runtime points at a defect in a policy. An empty chart means no evaluation errors in this range.

panels.title: HTTP requests by status
panels.description: Requests per second by status code, from the gin middleware. Deployments: 200 approve, 202 review, 403 deny, 409 access conflict, 422 failed evaluation. Access grants: 200 granted, 403 nothing granted, 409 conflict, 422 failed assert.

panels.title: Loaded policies
panels.description: Every policy that serves, by kind: each team's DeployApproval root and the AccessGrant root, with where its bundle came from (embedded, or a mounted directory). Not filtered by team, so the access root always shows.

panels.title: Policy reloads
panels.description: Bundle loads per interval by result, for the team and access bundles together. Polling only reloads when a directory changed, so an idle stack shows nothing here after startup.

panels.title: Decision traces · Tempo
panels.description: Traces containing a deploy or access span for the selected team. Open a trace to inspect the grants, decision, conditions and errors, then use its Logs link to open Loki.

panels.title: Decision logs · Loki
panels.description: Expand a decision log and follow View trace. Explore logs includes HTTP access logs and errors too.

panels.title: CPU profile · Pyroscope
panels.description: Whole-process CPU profile over the dashboard time range, including Sigil, HTTP handling and telemetry. Click a stack frame to focus it. Profiles upload every 15 seconds. Goroutine-leak capture also runs GC, and that cost is included.

panels.title: Runtime profile · Pyroscope
panels.description: Choose Runtime profile to inspect allocations, live heap, goroutines, mutex contention, blocking or detected goroutine leaks. Types appear after samples reach Pyroscope. Whole-process data over the selected time range; empty leak data is expected in a healthy process. Heap profiles are merged over the range; the RSS chart shows process memory.

panels.title: Observability targets · Alloy scrape health
panels.description: One means Alloy can scrape the target. This complements the Compose readiness checks; it does not assert end-to-end ingestion.

panels.title: deploygate · CPU and resident memory
panels.description: CPU is CPU-seconds per wall-clock second (cores). Memory is process RSS, not heap-only. These include telemetry overhead.
